rules.sentence: Seeds follow entry order, so the first player entered is seed 1. A bracket of four meets as 1 against 4, then 2 against 3. A bracket of eight meets as 1 against 8, 4 against 5, 3 against 6, then 2 against 7.
Name each round Quarterfinal, Semifinal or Final, and show it as "Round: NAME" while that round is played. A bracket of four has no Quarterfinal.
Quarterfinals are played on 4x4, semifinals on 6x6 and finals on 8x8.
Both players of a match play one board code, and every match in a tournament has a different board code.
markers: every match in a tournament has a different board code

rules.sentence: When both players of a match finish in the same number of moves, the lower active time wins, and if that is also equal the higher seed wins.
Tournament games never change best scores or the saved board size.
Every name a person types is stored and shown after trimming both ends, collapsing each run of inner whitespace to one space and normalizing to NFC.
A name has 2 to 20 Unicode code points after normalization. Anything else blocks the action and shows "Use 2 to 20 characters."
Names in one group compare without regard to case, after normalization. A repeat blocks the action and shows "Each name must be different."
New stored data uses a key of the form np3:THING, where THING is a lowercase plural noun for what is stored. Keys that already exist keep their names.
Every value a feature adds to browser storage is a JSON object with exactly two keys: "v", the number 3, and "items", the array of records.
A stored list keeps its newest 10 records and drops older ones when a new record is saved.
When browser storage is blocked, a feature keeps working in memory and shows "Progress won't be saved on this device." where its saved records would appear.
markers: Progress won't be saved on this device.

rules.sentence: A stored value that fails to parse or validate is treated as empty, without any error, and stays untouched until the next save replaces it.
markers: stays untouched until the next save

rules.sentence: Every new exported JSON object has a "format" of "neon-pairs/KIND", naming what it holds, and a whole-number "version", with its keys in alphabetical order at every level. Formats that already exist stay as they are.
An import with a field its format doesn't define shows "Unknown field: NAME." for the first such field and leaves the current state unchanged.
Ranked or bracket data is a table element with a caption and th scope="col" header cells.
The page has exactly one live region, the status paragraph in Game.tsx. New status text, such as whose turn it is, goes through that region.
When a feature replaces what the main area shows, focus moves to that screen's h2, which has tabindex="-1".
Leaving unfinished work asks first in a native dialog element with two buttons, Keep playing and Leave. Keep playing takes focus when it opens, and Escape keeps playing.
Every new control is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels at a 390 pixel wide viewport.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, new elements run no animation and no transition.
State is never shown by color alone, so a winner is marked with the text "(winner)" after the name.
Interface text has no exclamation marks.
markers: Interface text has no exclamation marks

rules.sentence: Counts of moves read "1 move" and "2 moves", and durations read M:SS, such as 0:07 and 12:30.
Only src/game/session/fresh-board.ts may call a random source. Everything else that needs randomness imports it from there.
Game code reads time only through the session clock. Only files in src/game/session/ may call performance.now, and no game code may use Date.
markers: no game code may use Date

rules.sentence: A feature lives in src/game/FEATURE/, and its rules live in src/game/FEATURE/rules.ts, which imports neither React nor any browser global.
A feature adds no entries to dependencies or devDependencies.
A feature's rules.ts has a rules.test.ts beside it.

superseded.statement: Stored data uses keys of the form neon-pairs.THING.v1, which is what the preferences key does today.
Confirmations use a div overlay with role="alertdialog" and a focus trap written by hand, with buttons Cancel and Discard.
Rankings and results are ordered lists, because they read well on phones.
Each feature owns its own aria-live region for its messages, shown as a toast.
Decorative animation is allowed under reduced motion when it lasts under 200 milliseconds.
Names may have 1 to 32 characters and are stored exactly as typed.

statements: Solo play is the only mode.
These are all the modules the game has.
Preferences are the only data written to the browser.
Progress snapshots are the only JSON the game exports.
The game writes one key to browser storage: `neon-pairs.preferences.v1`.
The game exports one kind of JSON, the progress snapshot.
There is no competition entry form, bracket view, participant model or tournament controller in `src/game/Game.tsx`.
